title: Retrieval practice produces more learning than elaborative studying with concept mapping.
central_claims: Retrieval practice outperforms elaborative concept mapping on delayed meaningful learning assessments.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. SSRP supplementary methods and Tables 1, 3 and 4
source_manifest.finding: Retrieval practice outperformed concept mapping on delayed recall: r=.384, p=.006, N=49. This is a bounded instructional comparison.

source_manifest.title: The effectiveness of concept mapping and retrieval practice as learning strategies in an undergraduate physiology course
source_manifest.finding: Classroom comparison found a retrieval-practice trend significant on one of four module examinations; original abstract read through Europe PMC.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating the replicability of social science experiments in Nature and Science between 2010 and 2015
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent replication reports positive significant focal results for both Aviezer and Karpicke/Blunt in Figure 1. Original-author reviewed protocols; not every original experiment was repeated.

source_manifest.title: Ritchie, Della Sala and McIntosh: Retrieval Practice, with or without Mind Mapping, Boosts Fact Learning in Primary School Children
source_manifest.finding: Independent in-class experiments adapted the retrieval/mapping comparison to 8–12-year-olds and geographical facts. Retrieval benefited recall through five weeks; mind mapping gave no consistent benefit. This simpler mapping task is not identical to original adult concept mapping.

source_manifest.title: Mayrhofer, Kuhbandner and Frischholz: Re-examining the testing effect as a learning strategy
source_manifest.finding: Preregistered N=230 comparison reproduces original verbatim recall advantage under original conditions. Adding memorization to concept mapping removes that advantage; inference performance does not favor retrieval. Single German text, one-week retention; authors acknowledge these boundaries.

source_manifest.title: American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation: Study Tips & Resources
source_manifest.finding: Official professional-exam guidance recommends self-testing and cites this paper among research supporting the advice. Demonstrates adoption into guidance, not measured candidate compliance or attribution of the whole testing-effect literature to this paper.
